hypothesis: An exact-timestamp-verified completed-minute cache for seven non-profit-lock V58 symbols, with every completed-bar profit-lock symbol uncached, can reduce shared-IP request pressure without changing route or exit semantics.
decision: Keep the live V58 runner unchanged and uncached. Correct the report-only cache candidate so a current in-progress candle cannot mask the absence of the exact just-completed timestamp. Continue to bypass every symbol derived from configured completed-bar profit-lock requirements, currently xyz:SP500. Reclassify the 1,440-minute watcher as first-published accepted-bar parity only: it cannot observe a later correction to an already emitted timestamp, prove provider-decision parity, or authorize a profit-lock cache cutover. Do not restart the active observer or request live promotion while its original prospective window is collecting.
falsifier: Reject the cache candidate if it reuses a response lacking the exact required completed timestamp; if any configured profit-lock symbol is cached; if the prospective accepted-bar prefix develops an internal gap, conflicting duplicate, or OHLCV mismatch; if same-input route decisions diverge; or if an authority-none run does not materially reduce HTTP 429 degradation and polling latency.
limitations: The accepted-bar watcher cannot detect a correction after telemetry has emitted that timestamp once.
The current active observer loaded the earlier all-symbol cache implementation and remains unchanged to preserve its prospective window.
No production V58 completed-candle revision has been observed; the late-revision risk is established by controller semantics and a synthetic test.
